To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) humans use episodic memory in reinforcement learning; 2) existing reinforcement learning tasks do not require episodic memory; 3) we define and implement a form of external episodic memory called Masked Episodic Memory (MEM) that allows agents to use it effectively.

episodic memory is an important component of general intelligence that is currently lacking in RL agents, and that a novel type of episodic memory called MEM enables RL agents to master a new RL task that requires it.

the problem of endowing RL agents with episodic memories.

we propose a new form of episodic memory for reinforcement learning agents that is based on key features of human memory, and evaluate it on the Concentration RL task.
we propose an external memory for reinforcement learning agents, which is modeled after key properties of human episodic memories, and show that it can be used to learn a new game.
the proposed method, MEM, is an effective and novel way of endowing RL agents with episodic memories that can be leveraged in a wide variety of RL tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed a new type of memory for reinforcement learning that is based on human episodic memory and is effective in a new RL task that we have designed.
episodic memory is useful for RL, and it is possible for RL agents to leverage episodic memory effectively.

The main takeaway from our work is that
episodic memory is an important feature to add to RL agents, and we provide a new benchmark for evaluating episodic memory in RL agents.
the lack of episodic memory is not a fundamental limitation of RL agents, and that it is possible to endow RL agents with episodic memories.
episodic memory, when properly defined, can be a key enabler for general RL.
